People's Majlis Committee Minutes

20th Meeting of the Economic Committee

12 October 2026

Venue: People's Majlis, A. Building (Committee Room 11)

Start time: 11:45
{Chaired by the Committee Chair; Member for Central Fuvahmulah constituency, Ali Fazad}

Chair speaking:
ﷺ. I welcome all members to the 20th meeting of the Economic Committee. On today's committee agenda is the interviewing of the persons whose names the President has sent for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, in accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act). In this regard, the memo the committee received contains 3 names. Our secretariat has checked all the requirements for these names and will also have sent you a paper. Now, regarding the issues in this, I will give the floor to the secretariat to clarify the information for you administratively.

Secretariat speaking:
As the rules state, it is after checking whether or not the requirements are met that the committee is informed. Now, you see. In accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act), in order to check whether the persons whose names the President has sent for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation meet the requirements set out in Article 9 of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act) for a person appointed to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, letters seeking clarification of information will have been sent administratively, in accordance with Article 223(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, to the Department of Judicial Administration, the Elections Commission, the Anti-Corruption Commission, the Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade and the Maldives Correctional Service. {Chaired by the Committee Chair; Member for Central Fuvahmulah constituency, Ali Fazad}

Chair speaking:
ﷺ. I welcome all members to the 20th meeting of the Economic Committee. On today's committee agenda is the interviewing of the persons whose names the President has sent for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, in accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act). In this regard, the memo the committee received contains 3 names. Our secretariat has checked all the requirements for these names and will also have sent you a paper. Now, regarding the issues in this, I will give the floor to the secretariat to clarify the information for you administratively.

Secretariat speaking:
As the rules state, it is after checking whether or not the requirements are met that the committee is informed. Now, you see. In accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act), in order to check whether the persons whose names the President has sent for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation meet the requirements set out in Article 9 of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act) for a person appointed to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, letters seeking clarification of information will have been sent administratively, in accordance with Article 223(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, to the Department of Judicial Administration, the Elections Commission, the Anti-Corruption Commission, the Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade and the Maldives Correctional Service. After reviewing the information sent by those institutions and the CVs of those persons sent with the President's letter, we note that the requirements set out in Article 9 of the aforementioned law are met by Mr. Ahmed Shafneez, Bageechaage, S. Hulhudhoo, and Mr. Ahmed Mausoom, Vimayares. However, the President's

letter, in our review of the CV of Ms. Mariyam Jaidha sent with it, we noted that, of the requirements set out in Article 9 of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act), she has not obtained from an institution recognised by the government a master's degree or a qualification of an equivalent level in a field related to economics, finance, business or tax, as set out in paragraph (a) of that Article. Therefore, in checking from the information sent with the President's letter whether she has at least 10 years of experience working in a field related to government finance, as set out in that paragraph, looking at the period that can be considered relevant to the requirement, the period she worked at the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority is 9 years, 11 months and 22 days; and although she has included as experience the work she did at CDE Private Limited from November 2011 to August 2012, that work was a job held at a private company, and the work done in that job is stated to have been collecting socio-economic statistics and writing analysis reports, which we do not consider to be work in a field related to government finance; therefore it is noted that she does not have at least 10 years of experience in a field related to government finance. As a general principle, we check whether the requirements are met against the information sent with the President's letter and the information sent by the aforementioned institutions in reply to the letters sent to them. Ms. Mariyam Jaidha has informed us by phone that she wishes to submit additional documents showing that she has worked in a field related to government finance. Therefore, we request the committee to decide whether to give her the opportunity to submit those documents. In addition, I note that, in accordance with Article 223(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, we published an announcement to check whether there were any public complaints about the persons whose names the President sent for appointment to the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, and when the period of that announcement ended, the committee had not received any complaint regarding any of them. Now, she has requested an opportunity to submit additional documents. Now, there is no such information in the CV either. So, normally, if there is no supporting

documentation for information written in a CV, we call and obtain that information. But what she said was that she wishes to submit information that is not in the CV either. So I request the committee to decide whether or not to give her the opportunity to submit that information.

Chair speaking:
So, we first give the floor to Ismail Nizar.

Member for North Feydhoo constituency Ismail Nizar speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. As the secretariat just said, among the three persons who had applied, it is Ms. Mariyam Jaidha who does not meet this requirement. So, rather than an additional opportunity, what I think is that we should proceed with the interview matters with the persons who now meet this requirement. So, I propose that this interview proceed in that way. That is my proposal. Thank you. (After a moment) Yes! I will add to my proposal. There is now a request for an additional opportunity to submit these documents. But this process would again become very long. And if we give an opportunity like this, I believe this could even create a precedent. What I think is that we proceed with our interviews with those submitted who meet the requirements. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Yes! I second the proposal made by the honourable Member for North Feydhoo constituency, Ismail Nizar.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Ms. Mariyam Jaidha, Gasdhoshuge, K. Dhiffushi. In the letter we received from the President's Office she met the requirements; we received it with the requirements met as far as the President's Office was concerned. Then, as part of how we work in the committee, when we checked in the committee the additional matters we have to look at, what we noted was that she was 10 days short, 10 days short of completing 10 years. What I would say is that Jaidha is now pointing out that if Jaidha had the opportunity to submit additional documents she would be able to do that, those documents, that opportunity exists. What I just want to say is that if the President's Office had checked this matter as thoroughly as it needed to be checked, I think Jaidha would also have got that opportunity at that time to complete or send that document, or else it would have concluded that the requirements were not met without our having to come to the point of discussing this a second time. From some information we have received, Jaidha says that certain kinds of documents cannot be added to a form that is filled in at the President's Office. So, going forward too, I think it would be good, and it would probably make things easier for all of us, to share this matter with the President's Office. In a letter sent from the President's Office the requirements were met, and when we noted these matters, the requirements were not met and this person ended up being left out. I think it is something we really must do to inform them so that this does not happen, so that this experience does not happen to another person in future. Perhaps, among these three persons, she might even turn out to be the most suitable person for this, once the interviews are done. We do not know. I am saying this because it could not be taken as far as an interview. In reality, the reason the committee cannot now give us that opportunity is due to very many reasons, as we noted administratively in the committee and in various other ways.

So, I take this opportunity to request that we must somehow inform the President's Office of how this happened. Otherwise such things may be repeated again. So, she was 10 days short of 10 years. If, when she was just 10 days short of 10 years, this had been noted at that time, I think this would have been concluded much better than this. So, that is the point I wanted to note. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, Abdulla Sodig.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. Considering the point raised by the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Nazil, I too want to note that it is a very important matter, as at this stage Jaidha was left out without getting an opportunity even though she had said she would make an additional submission. It seems that was lost because it was not checked that thoroughly at the earlier stage. So, that needs to be noted. And this person is a young person, and when I looked, she has achieved very complete success at every stage, even during her studies. However, when something like this is left out of one's own CV, it is the kind of point that could also raise questions about the carefulness of a person taking charge of such a state post, when a plus point of her own CV was left out. That too is a point that can be noted. So, I note that I second what the honourable Member Nazil proposed. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
As proposed by the honourable Member for North Feydhoo constituency, Ismail Nizar, and seconded by the honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed, those who are in favour of proceeding with the interviews of the two persons at numbers one and two of this letter, in light of all the information obtained when our secretariat checked that they meet the requirements,

are asked to vote. (Voting) So, it is passed by consensus of the members present in this committee at this time. Then, in this committee, the honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, has proposed, and the honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, Abdulla Sodig, has seconded that proposal, Nazil's view. That is, that we administratively inform the President's Office of how this problem arose with the matters that come regarding the requirements of such persons. So, I also say that this matter be taken forward administratively. Now, from this point we will proceed with the interviews. The first interview will be with Mr. Ahmed Shafneez, Bageechaage, S. Hulhudhoo. (After a moment) السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. What we are proceeding with at this time is the interview conducted by this Economic Committee because Mr. Ahmed Shafneez, Bageechaage, S. Hulhudhoo, has applied for the post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation in accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act), you see. So, first of all, I ask Ahmed Shafneez to give an introduction of himself and to introduce to us in the committee the reason he is interested in this post of Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, or about this post.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. الحمد لله رب العالمين. والصلاة والسلام على رسول الله وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. I thank the honourable members of the committee very much for giving me this opportunity. My full name is Ahmed Shafneez. My permanent address is S. Hulhudhoo, Bageechaage. Now, to introduce myself, first of all, at around the age of ten I moved to Malé to obtain education. Since then and up to today I have been living in Malé. Now, first, looking at my educational life, after moving to Malé I joined Madhrasathul Ahmadhiyya. After doing O Level there, I then joined CHSE, and after doing A Level there I went out into the working environment. After going out, I first

worked at the Capital Market Development Section, the then Capital Market Development Section of the MMA. After working there for about a year, I got a scholarship to pursue higher education. With that opportunity I went to the International Islamic University of Malaysia. There I obtained a degree in economics. After that, again about six months later, I did a master's in finance at the same university. Then, after completing my studies, I came to Malé in 2012 and first joined a private company. After working there as head of finance for about three months, I got the opportunity to join MIRA, where I now work. I joined MIRA in 2012, first as a deputy manager of its finance section. Having worked there since, today I am the head of MIRA's Administration and Finance Department. It has now been about seven years in this post, since I have been working here. Now, my main current responsibilities are formulating MIRA's budget and preparing MIRA's financial statements. Also, overseeing MIRA's administrative work and overseeing procurement work are in my mandate. In addition, my work includes overseeing the enterprise risk management function and overseeing business continuity management work. Besides this, what I most want to note is that, in the way work is organised at MIRA, we have committees formed for every matter. So, as a senior executive, I also get the opportunity to take part in those committees. Accordingly, in every committee, regarding that matter, for example even when the Commissioner makes a decision, decisions are made after very extensive consultation in those committees. In that regard, I have worked, for example, as a member of the Human Resource Committee. And likewise I am also a member of the Risk Management Steering Committee. So, because of working in such committees, we get [to see] all of MIRA's overall work

and opportunities to take part in decision making. So, over the past seven years I will have been very much involved in MIRA's work across a very wide area. In addition, MIRA is an institution that does a great deal of work, continuously, for the advancement of its staff. In that regard, training is given to our staff both in the Maldives and abroad. Accordingly, I too have been getting, up to today, opportunities to take part in various trainings in the Maldives and abroad. For example, I have had opportunities to take part in various trainings abroad and in the Maldives in fields such as compliance risk management, business continuity or enterprise risk management, and digitalisation. So, because every MIRA employee gets such opportunities, I have been working at MIRA with great happiness up to today. As we see it, MIRA is an institution that has a very good working environment even for people entering the workforce for the first time, and, relative to the Maldives, it is an institution whose work the public very much accepts, that is very trusted, and whose staff's integrity and commitment the public very much accepts; therefore I still want to see whether I can get an opportunity at MIRA to work in a wider area than this. Therefore, in the hope of getting that opportunity, I applied for this post. Yes! Thank you.

Chair speaking:
After the self-introduction, I will now open the floor for members to ask further questions. Honourable Member for North Thinadhoo constituency, Saudulla Hilmy.

Member for North Thinadhoo constituency Saudulla Hilmy speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Welcome, Shafneez. My question is, if you come to this post, how much assurance

can you give us that you will remain in this post until the end of the term, I mean until the end of five years? I say this because in some cases, if a good offer comes from elsewhere, something like leaving, could that happen?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. As I said in my introduction too, I have spent about 14 years at MIRA. After I finished my studies and joined MIRA, I joined very new, I first joined the workforce at MIRA, roughly. However, I note with great happiness that MIRA is an institution whose leadership at that time very much encouraged us, even people newly joining employment, by giving training, to come to posts like this. So, in reality too, in order to show the staff under me as well that I am a good example of that, if I get this post, after completing my term fully and successfully, and in addition, showing the staff under me the example that my former superiors showed, in order to give them the assurance that they too will get such opportunities, working continuously for their advancement is something I very much want. So, I give a firm assurance that I will complete the five years.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Welcome, Ahmed Shafneez. The question I want to ask is, from the information received and as you also noted in your introduction, you have worked at MIRA for a very long time. So, overall, regarding the problems MIRA now faces and

the things that could be done to take it further, I believe you would be one of the people who knows best. In that regard, if you get this post, what things would you do to improve results compared to now? Is there such a plan? If there is, could you describe such a plan in detail?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. As Article 10 of the Tax Administration Act stands, the responsibility of the Deputy Commissioner is to provide the Commissioner with the assistance needed and, in a situation where there is no Commissioner, to carry out that responsibility. In that capacity, I too already have in my plan some things I have thought of doing. In that regard, as I believe, one of the biggest challenges MIRA now faces is the challenge of retaining our staff, especially technical staff. You probably know that since tax was introduced in the Maldives up to today, the demand for this work in the private sector, I mean the demand for tax experts, has risen very greatly. And above all, our staff's tax knowledge, as I said earlier, is being developed very greatly by giving trainings. So, when they have been developed, because of the demand for them from there in the private sector, we in reality face very big challenges in retaining staff. So, in my thinking, in addition to giving our staff, especially technical staff, training to increase their human capacity further, I am planning to think of ways in which they can be retained and to implement those things. Then we, another very big challenge at MIRA now is, although we first started MIRA with about a hundred staff, there are now more than three hundred staff. However, our space constraints are not, on the other hand, increasing [unclear] to the same extent. So, we then also

see that in reality this also has a very big negative effect on retaining staff. So, we also have in the plan arrangements to see whether things can be arranged so that staff at MIRA can work in a somewhat more comfortable environment. Then, as a third matter, especially at MIRA, we now very much want to provide services in cooperation with the actual taxpayers. So, many things are planned to strengthen as much as possible the relationship that now exists with taxpayers and to change how taxpayers view MIRA. In particular, we will already have started a "Gulhigen MIRA" campaign as well. Under it too, through the trust taxpayers place in us and the work done together with them, we believe that tax compliance also increases greatly to the extent that the relationship and trust between taxpayers and the tax enforcement office is maintained. So, we will also work on those things with a very big focus. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Velidhoo constituency, Mohamed Abbas.

Member for Velidhoo constituency Mohamed Abbas speaking:
Yes! Thank you very much, Chair. Welcome, Shafneez. My main question is, since you are someone who is still working at MIRA, with experience, and who knows very well everything about how the Maldives' tax system is now going, in reality now, since some days ago up to now, what is happening is that very rapid changes are being brought to tax laws. Not very long periods are given for implementation either. Earlier, six months or a year would be given. So, in reality, large taxpayers, large companies paying large amounts of tax, because they have staff of various levels to match, get information on these matters very fully. In particular, MIRA provides all this information by e-mail

[by e-mail]. And to some extent through the media as well. However, familiarising people with the tax payment laws, or the information on this matter in the fullest way it should be received, is still not that clear to the small and medium businesses. As a result, sometimes when audits and such are carried out in other atolls, those persons are also given some degree of relief. But fines are also being incurred very heavily; in ignorance they are fined large amounts, and it even reaches the point where small and medium businesses collapse. However, MIRA does give relief in accordance with the law and within the powers the Commissioner of Taxation has. So, in future, is there any thinking at all about establishing a system through which these citizens can be given information on tax across as wide an area as possible? That is the question.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. We have a strategic plan formulated. One main strategy in it is familiarising the public with tax. In that regard, we are doing a great deal of work to familiarise taxpayers with tax laws and regulations. Accordingly, we have a training centre, and under the Tax Academy we also run a great many trainings for taxpayers. For example, as soon as a new taxpayer registers with MIRA, we run trainings for them. In addition, running training sessions in schools, and likewise our teams travelling to various islands of the Maldives and conducting information sessions in those islands, are also things we are already doing. Now, we note very much now that, earlier, when we worked to provide that information to taxpayers through, for example, radio and TV, it was very effective. However, now that may perhaps not be the best way. For example, instead of TV and radio, many people now use social media, right? So, we are now also making very great use of those channels

to give information to taxpayers. So, as you said, we too believe that, to increase tax compliance, in reality giving taxpayers the information they need is one of the most important things; because we believe that, MIRA is continuously doing that, you see. And in the future too, as I said, the things that can be done to further improve the approach we are now taking have been discussed in our technical teams and planned for implementation. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, Abdulla Sodig.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Shafneez, Ahmed Shafneez, having worked at MIRA for a very long time, working for seven years, you will have faced very many things. Very many problems; the seven years was in the current post, wasn't it? 14 years, right? Having spent a total of 14 years, having spent them in various posts, you will have faced various different things. In resolving such things, sitting on the risk management committee, you will also have taken part in resolving very many such problems that arose then. So, on taking charge of this post, if you get this post, what do you see as the biggest issue that could arise, that you could face, the difficulty that could arise? Could there be such a difficulty, that is one question. And I noted that in the introduction you only mentioned your address and did not give much of a family introduction, being married, having children, that kind of introduction. To some extent the person, I think that is something we too wanted to hear in the introduction. There will be things it shows too. And could any family influence be exerted on coming to this post? Would there be? That too is something I want to know, you see. Thank you.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see, honourable member. So, I will begin with the second question, you see. I have a wife and two children. And in my family, on the other hand, neither my father nor my mother is in business. And my wife's family is also not a business family. However, my elder brothers do some business to some extent. However, I am very certain that such influence will not affect my work at all. As an assurance of that, I would say that at MIRA, from the very beginning, as I said in my introduction too, the reason MIRA's work has remained, up to today, that of an institution the public trusts very much is in reality the policies implemented by our leaders at that time, I mean the way the governance structure was actually built. For example, I think we would all accept that if the head running a place is given full authority to make decisions, there may be a chance of things not going in the best way; so the thing our leaders at that time did, giving it the highest priority, is actually a good governance structure, plus things are arranged such that no MIRA decision is made in a way that a particular individual, a particular person, decides it because they want a particular thing. For example, even when looking at doing an audit, or looking at going to investigate a place, or to take action against a taxpayer or make a decision, to make a decision regarding a taxpayer, very many steps are gone through. As I said earlier, there are committees for every matter. It is after consultation in those committees and their advice going to the Commissioner that this decision is made. So, up to today, actually one reason I am happiest at MIRA is that in reality MIRA has remained, up to today, an institution the public trusts very much, with very high integrity. So, I assure you that there will be no such family influence. Then, the question the honourable member asked as the first question was the biggest problem that could arise, right? As we believe, because taxpayers in reality do not get the full information they actually should get, sometimes they face difficulties like this in preparing tax statements as well as possible, or in calculating the amount of money

to be paid. So, as we believe, the most important thing is actually that people's accounts; in the Maldives there is a self-assessment system. So, they have to pay tax based on these things, the amount they submit to MIRA, for example, after preparing the tax statement. However, after that, through a risk assessment, we have to see whether they need to be audited, for example, or whether to proceed by engaging further with them to put things right. Instead of that, as I see it, designing things in a way that reduces such problems or audits as much as possible is something we give great priority to. In that regard, for example, giving taxpayers information extensively. Engaging with them and, as much as possible, instead of feedback, giving feedforward, telling them in advance the ways they can put things right; I believe the issues I mentioned can be resolved that way. Thank you, you see.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Welcome, Ahmed Shafneez. Shafneez, in your introduction you first mentioned that, besides MIRA, you worked at another company. Which place was that?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see, honourable member. When I first came back after finishing my studies, I worked at Island Broadcasting Company Private Limited for 3 months.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:

The responsibility of the DCG, the Deputy Commissioner General, is to ease the Commissioner General's work or to do the things that person says. That is how it stands legally. And, in a situation where there is no CG, to carry out the CG's responsibilities. How much certainty is there that you could carry out the CG's responsibilities, and, in your view, does the current CG have that trust and confidence that Shafneez can do it?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see, honourable member. When I applied for this post too, one of the very first things I looked at was what my responsibility would be, right? So, as I said earlier too, Article 10 of the Tax Administration Act provides that, in addition to doing the work assigned by the Commissioner General, [the Deputy] bears the Commissioner's responsibilities in a situation where there is no Commissioner. Now, I have probably repeated very often that decision making at MIRA is done in a very organised way, with decisions made after matters are discussed in committees. So, because I too have taken part in very many committees over roughly the past seven years, as I said, I know how that workflow goes and so on. So, I have a lot of confidence that, for example, in a situation where I have to bear the CG's responsibilities, there are very technical people under me. MIRA has very technical, very high-integrity staff. So, I am also certain that I will get their full support. Given that, I am very certain that carrying out such a responsibility would not be any difficulty for me at all. Thank you, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! The CG, in fact the Commissioner General of MIRA, is someone who has the power to decide everything. Now, here I believe that Shafneez, having spent many days at MIRA in particular,

that will be clear. What I basically want to ask is whether, within MIRA's departments, there is enough trust in Shafneez that, when it reaches the point where Shafneez carries out the CG's responsibilities, they will accept that the decisions Shafneez makes are the best, that those decisions are the best decisions. How close are you within the departments? What is the relationship like? Will they accept the decisions you make?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see, honourable member. I, we MIRA staff are a team that works very much together. In particular, many of those in the executive team, it may now be about ten years that we have been working together. So, every one of us is well acquainted, it is a team with a very close relationship, a really good team with very good teamwork. However, as I said, rather than such a relationship leading to any negative effect or undesirable things being done in the working environment, we work as a very professional institution. So, what I mean is, as I believe, if I am chosen for this post, I will get the full support of the executive team along with me in this.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Shafneez just noted that the current CG is the former DCG. At that time a lot of work will have been done together with that person. Do you have that person's trust as well to do this?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. As you said, the current Commissioner is our former Deputy Commissioner. And in addition, before becoming Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, that person also worked with us as an Assistant Commissioner, as a DG, and at director

level. So, I have no doubt about that, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Some people, the public, [see MIRA] as a place where political influence comes and goes. It is something talked about in the islands. For example, what we once heard, about how a week after a gold money box was given to Gasim Ibrahim, he was said to be someone owing MIRA 1 billion rufiyaa in tax, was arrested and put in jail, and political things happened. Shafneez was at MIRA then too. To what extent, within the past governments, two or three governments, within the governments that have passed, how much effort was made by governments to exert political influence on MIRA? Do you believe there was such effort? If so, who did it?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. As I said first, in the introduction too, MIRA's work is very much designed such that matters are not arranged so that things are decided according to a particular individual or according to orders that come in like that. Even to make decisions there are steps we have to follow. Who will make the decision. How someone can be shortlisted for an audit. And, as you said, for example, if an award is given to someone, how that award is given too; all the work is done by a committee. So, as I believe, I do not believe that such influence would come into MIRA's work. As for the specific case you mentioned, at that time I was working as a Director General, mostly doing administrative work, so I cannot say anything directly about it.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:

Thank you, Chair, for giving the opportunity. In working with the Tax Appeal Tribunal, how much cooperation is there, is there a particular standard for how you work? What I mean is, is there work you necessarily have to do together with them? Or is your work entirely separate?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. The Tax Appeal Tribunal and MIRA are two separate independent institutions created by law. So, we also do our work very independently. However, for example, when the staff or members of the Tax Appeal Tribunal request training, training on particular tax laws or on a regulation, we do give that assistance, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Thank you. Very complete, you see. Thank you very much for answering every question so completely.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for North Feydhoo constituency, Ismail Nizar.

Member for North Feydhoo constituency Ismail Nizar speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Welcome, Mr. Ahmed Shafneez. You have answered very many questions. I note you as a very competent person. Now, my question is, taking into account the changes coming to the world economy and the Maldivian economy, what are the risks the tax system could face? And if you get this opportunity, how will you mitigate them? Thank you.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see, honourable member. As you said, this is a time when the world economy is suffering very negative effects. The Middle East crisis or the Russia-Ukraine war, every such thing will have a negative impact, especially on an economy like ours that depends on tourism. And every negative effect such things have on the economy will also have negative effects on tax. Therefore, as I believe, at this juncture, for example, not receiving tax in line with our projections and such things are risks that could arise. So, to mitigate those things, as I see it, we must take measures for that starting from now. In that regard, working to increase the compliance of taxpayers who are now within our tax net, and working to recover money owed to the state that has not been received; through such things, I think doing the work needed to meet our revenue projections may be important. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
To the honourable Member for Kurendhoo constituency, Mohamed Shamin Habeeb.

Member for Kurendhoo constituency Mohamed Shamin Habeeb speaking:
Thank you. Welcome! I have just one question. Those who do not pay tax are very many. Those who commit tax fraud are also very many. In addition, I think the state is losing the most income because foreign businesses have increased in the Maldives, making tax collection difficult and not being monitored, that is what I believe. This is something the public, and especially businesspeople, Maldivian businesspeople, talk about very often. And it is also something whose solution comes very slowly. The monitoring of this, something I always say is that this monitoring is not good. What I mean is it is not carried out at the required

speed. Therefore, even before being selected for this post, I think, as a person working in that field, you probably have a vision that we want it to be like this. It would be good if it were like this. As you said, I too believe decisions will be made by committees or through consultation. But there will also be things you personally believe. Foreign businesspeople coming and doing business here, not paying tax, and doing business in Maldivians' names, and in this way doing business in cash, and then keeping that money and taking it abroad; I think all these things are now very commonly seen in the newspapers too. So, what is Shafneez's view, and to do this, how would it be good to bring [changes] to the regulations currently being implemented, or in what way? Or by bringing what kind of change could there be a way that Maldivians doing business in general are not harmed and the tax income MIRA receives also increases? It would be very good if Shafneez gave his view on this. Thank you.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. As you said, we too see foreigners doing business like this in Malé and even running small businesses in some islands. Now, part of MIRA's work is to look at the businesses carried on in the Maldives and, if those persons, in the business they do, fall within the thresholds set in the tax laws, to register them for tax and check that they pay tax accordingly, and to ensure that. Now, we have a compliance team in Malé too. And in our regional offices too, those teams are always going and checking, as it were, all the businesses of that atoll, and checking whether those persons act on their tax responsibilities, as I said, in accordance with the laws and regulations; we are working continuously to ensure that. So, as you said, there is still, I think, a great deal of business done using cash, for example. If such things happen largely outside the banking system, those transactions are actually not properly captured,

right? So, we are still slowly travelling towards a largely cashless system, aren't we? I think if the whole economy is transformed so that those businesses too make great use of cards or bank transfers and cash transactions can be reduced, then, as you said, the problem as a whole, on the other hand, matters of tax fraud too will be resolved to a great extent. And I think the biggest solution to the very problem in the question you asked would actually come from developing ways for information to be exchanged from one government office to another as systematically as possible, in real time or near real time. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Yes! Honourable Member for Kanditheemu constituency, Ameen Faisal.

Member for Kanditheemu constituency Ameen Faisal speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. I too have just one question. As a member also noted earlier, in this 20th Majlis too we have brought very big changes to various tax rates. And in particular, the type of tax we most recently passed in the Majlis, we have [heard] very strong criticism, especially from the tourism industry, that they face very big challenges. And because of it, our tourism business is also facing very big challenges, and very many people have concerns. And the government too now seems to be thinking of reconsidering it. Looking at the various tax amounts brought recently, what is the Maldivian economy now, are these amounts the best amounts, or to improve further, to improve our economy further, what is the best way? How do you view this destination tax decided to be levied recently, and these things? Is it something we can do? Or, at this time,

given how our economy is, is it something good to take a further step, what is it as Shafneez sees it?

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Yes! Thank you, you see, honourable member. In the Maldives, every tax is introduced, or decided to be introduced, after very extensive research, consultation and studies at the policy level. And the specific tax you noted, for example the change brought to GST, taxing GST based on the destination principle. That too, it is actually the Finance Ministry that sets tax policy. Whether a change is brought to a rate or a change is brought to the tax base, those are policy changes. So, MIRA's responsibility is that, once they set the tax policy, submit it to the Majlis as a bill and the law is passed, our responsibility is the work of enforcing that law. As I see it, this destination-based GST is an already established way being used in developed countries of the world, taxing GST that way. So, as I said earlier too, I believe that the decisions made on the policy side by the Ministry of Finance after very extensive study of the Maldivian economy and this economic environment of the Maldives would be the best decisions. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
So, we will conclude at this point the interview we have been conducting with Ahmed Shafneez. So, I thank you very much for coming to the committee and for the information you shared with us. And wishing Ahmed Shafneez success in the future ahead, thank you very much, you see.

Ahmed Shafneez speaking:
Thank you, you see.

(After a moment)

Chair speaking:
السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ. What we in this Economic Committee are proceeding with is [the interview held] because Mr. Ahmed Mausoom, V. Miares, has applied for the post of Deputy Commissioner of Taxation in accordance with Article 8(a) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act). So, we will proceed at this time with the interview conducted by the committee. So, first of all, I give the opportunity for Ahmed Mausoom to share with us in the committee an introduction and [why he is] interested in this post.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيْمِ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ. I thank all you honourable members for giving me this opportunity. I am Ahmed Mausoom. I have obtained education in various different fields. Accordingly, after completing A Level at Majeedhiyya, I obtained an accounting diploma from the then Institute of Management. After that, abroad, I obtained a first degree in computing. Then, two or three years ago, I obtained a master's in management from Villa College. I have served in various government offices and private companies for about twenty-five years. Of that, I have spent about eight years in the government's finance and economic offices. I see myself as someone who makes decisions responsibly and thoughtfully, who has the ability to work with staff of various levels in any environment, who is accountable in situations where one has to be accountable for matters, and who very much loves integrity. And I believe that, in light of the education and experience I have, I can provide some kind of

assistance in achieving MIRA's goals. Now, the main reason I am trying to move to MIRA, to join MIRA, is that a large part of my career will have been in service to that field as well. In addition, I believe that having a good, transparent tax system is very important for the country's development, you see. In that regard, for example, the services we provide and the projects we run are run with money received from the tax system. So, using the knowledge and skills I have learned, what I want is to further strengthen MIRA's management, and to win the public's, what should I say, the public's trust for that institution, and to pave the way for the state to receive adequate revenue, you see.

Chair speaking:
I open the floor for members to ask Ahmed Mausoom further questions. Abdulla Sodig, of North Hithadhoo constituency.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. Welcome, Ahmed Mausoom. Yes! I too looked at Mausoom's CV. Yes! In the introduction just now too you noted the independent things [roles] in which you have served the state in various fields. But in the introduction you did not mention anything about your family. So, one question is, with a short introduction about your family, if you come to this post, would there be any influence from any family member? That is one question. Yes! After that question is finished I will continue.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! Up to now I have carried out my jobs very independently. So, no influence can be exerted on me by anyone, you see.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:

Regarding the family.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
I was born in Addu Atoll. But I am now living on the Malé register, you see.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Are you married? Do you have children?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! Yes! Yes! I am married and I have 2 children, you see. Yes! Excuse me!

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
You have noted that there will be no family influence. In carrying out the responsibilities of the post of Deputy Commissioner General, I also noted from the CV that you moved from the Finance Ministry at the time MIRA was formed and worked in its IT then. And having been there for every year, about six years, you would know the difficulties there, those that existed then. You may not know about now. However, now you note that you are coming to the second most senior post there. On coming, in carrying out the responsibilities of this post, given how things are there now, and given how MIRA's work is currently organised, what are the difficulties that could arise? Could you point them out?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! Now MIRA generally operates under the government's tax policy. And a representative of the Minister will also sit on MIRA's board. The board will be formulating the principles, regulations and laws by which MIRA must be run

. Then, our responsibility is to run MIRA's affairs in the way the board determines, you see. We do not have much opportunity in policy matters, you see.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for North Thinadhoo constituency, Saudulla Hilmy.

Member for North Thinadhoo constituency Saudulla Hilmy speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Welcome, Mausoom. I have 2 questions. The first question is, with the changes coming to the economic situation of the Maldives, what do you see as the biggest challenge that could arise in the tax field in the distant future? And how will you prepare for it? The first question, you see.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Thank you. One could talk at great length on this subject. But as I believe, we now need to do a proper scientific study of the taxes that exist now, you see. Whether those taxes are right. Whether the amounts set are the right amounts. For example, I could increase their rates. But whether a permanent benefit can be produced from that; that is, as I think, we need to study all the taxes that exist now. For example, take as one example a tourist resort, a safari and a guesthouse, you see. These 3 investments are each a different investment. And their return will also be high [unclear]. The risk will also differ, the return will also differ. But we do not see much difference in how tax is levied. And that is, for example, whether it is a wealthy person who may run a guesthouse, or an ordinary person. That compensation needs to be given. We need to develop businesses as the first thing. Only then will we get tax from those places tomorrow, you see. That is how I see it.

Member for North Thinadhoo constituency Saudulla Hilmy speaking:
The second question is mainly linked to the things you just mentioned. That is, to strengthen the tax system, do you note any amendment that needs to be brought to the tax laws, including the Tax Administration Act? Just now.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! I, as I noted earlier too, we are not the ones who decide policy matters. However, I do have my views on that matter, you see. For example, I would say that with the green tax, I do not know why it is taken from the guest, you see. I think it should be taken from things that harm the environment, or from those who take part in them. The reason green tax should be taken from every guest coming to the Maldives is not, on the other hand, that clear to me. I think, for example, as I believe, those taxes could be taken from activities of the kind that harm the Maldives. But, as I said earlier, a scientific study of that too would be needed, you see. That is one thing. Then, as I noted earlier, it is also like that in the areas of tourism tax. And there is also room to further improve the matters on which tax is now levied. For example, there are matters by which very many parties are able to escape from it. I need to work to resolve those matters. Then, I think, good revenue could be generated going forward.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh.

Member for Funadhoo constituency Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:
Thank you, Chair. Welcome, Ahmed Mausoom. My question is, of the revenue that is about seventy-plus percent of the Maldivian state's budget, the tax share is about, as the tax share

it stands at seventy-plus percent. A very large amount. And with this amount standing like this, there is still tax at MIRA as pending, or receivables, larger than what PSIP spends in these budgets. That is, as tax receivables and non-tax receivables. Within the economy that has been recovering after COVID, roughly, following that, at the end of 2021 an amount greater than ten billion was in receivables. That amount kept growing and growing, reaching 14.2 in 2022. 18.9 in 2023. Then in 2024 there has been a decrease of two billion. In reality this is a very large amount when looking at this state budget in the Maldives. And if one looks at the tax share of the budget, the revenue share, it is an even larger percent. So, do you have any thinking to reduce this amount, or to bring to it, or a solution for this, or a plan for this? What is the solution that can be brought to this? Or what is the work that can be done for this, to reduce this figure? Thank you.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Now there are also difficulties in this, you see. For example, I would say that there are procedures that have to be followed, you see, in recovering unpaid taxes. For example, we go to the tribunal, the tribunal's decisions go to the court stage, and in such matters there would be no set period that can be stated directly. We have to find a way to speed up that system. And I cannot state at this time directly anything that can be done about it. I would first have to assess the current pendings, how, what issue is involved. God willing, I will see whether those matters can be resolved to the extent of my [unclear] and capability. But I cannot personally solve directly the things that are legal, you see.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Welcome, Mausoom. The question I want to ask is, now tax, what we very often hear is that MIRA does not do adequate work in collecting tax from businesses in the islands within the atolls. And we also get information that some shops, some businesses commit a great deal of tax fraud. So, if Ahmed Mausoom is selected for the post you have applied for, what are the policies you would adopt to expand the work in the atolls beyond the work now being done, and to recover the money those parties owe? What work would you do?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Thank you. Yes! That is a very big task, you see. For example, in the islands, in small islands, it could be difficult for us administratively to set up tax offices directly and do that work. However, we will look, for example in those islands, we now also have technology, you see, at ways of providing those services by keeping even a focal point in those islands. For example, we can also give information online. So, I will focus on the area you mentioned, God willing, if I get that opportunity, you see.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. Welcome, Ahmed Mausoom. The post Mausoom has applied for is the post of Deputy Commissioner General. The responsibility of the Deputy Commissioner General is to assist the Commissioner General in that person's work. How much certainty does Mausoom have that, in a situation where there is no Commissioner General, that

institution, the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority, how much certainty is there that the responsibility of that work could be carried out most completely?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! Thank you. Now, I am an employee who has been working at that office roughly since the Department of Inland Revenue was formed. And when MIRA was formed, I was an employee who was active at the forefront in the move to MIRA, you see. In drafting the administrative law at that time, I am one of the 3 people who worked with the lawyers of the President's Office, you see. Yet I am not a legal person either. So, I think other parties would place that trust in me because I have that capability, right? So, I have full certainty that if I am entrusted with the job, I will be able to carry it out, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Now the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority, you just talked about its formation. Now that it has come into being, there, as I believe, previously too we in this committee have discussed and talked with the Inland Revenue Authority about very many matters included in this committee's mandate. And the committee, the current CG too is a CG we brought after interviewing in this committee, and the CG before that too was a CG we brought after interviewing in this committee. And a fair amount of work has been done here with the members brought to the Tax Appeal Tribunal, brought to the board. How familiar is Mausoom with the changes brought to MIRA, then and now, especially the amendments brought to laws, brought to the Tax Administration Act? What do you say about the most recent amendment brought?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
The most recent amendment you mentioned, that is taxing foreign tourist agents, right?

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! No problem, that amendment is also OK.

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Yes! I think that amendment is something that should have been done earlier too, you see. It is now somewhat delayed, right? But still it is something that has to be done. But my view is that, in bringing tax laws, it is good to bring changes to laws after doing scientific studies and properly studying their impact. Now, I, the administrative law, more or less as a whole, is something we drafted. There will now be some changes in it. The way the board is now constituted is a good way. And the process of appointing the Commissioner General and Deputy Commissioner General has also been improved. That matter is not as it was before, you see. So, there are such changes, you see. And since I am not directly involved in that these days, I may perhaps not know directly, letter by letter, what is in the law, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
With the Tax Appeal Tribunal formed and the tribunal operating under a separate law, MIRA's, for example if you were MIRA's DCG and even if you had to temporarily take charge as CG, what are the relationships that should exist between MIRA and the tribunal? In which areas, and to what extent, within what standard, will the relationship between these two institutions or these two offices exist?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
What the tribunal actually decides is whether MIRA's decisions are wrong or right; it reviews that. So, we have to provide them the information they need easily. Not necessarily

the way we made the decision. The information the persons concerned need; even though it is run as a separate institution, I see that by our working sufficiently together with them it will become easier to conclude those cases.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Now, regarding integrity, we ask in this way in our interviews with all persons. Has Mausoom previously worked to any extent in private, other particular companies?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
Recently I have been at Villa, you see. But as I said earlier, I am an independent person. If you look at my record up to now, you will know that no improper thing of any kind has been noted against me at any office, you see. I still have that assurance. It will be there in the future too, you see.

Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil speaking:
Yes! Another question is, very often there is talk of a great deal of money. Especially as tax, as the honourable Member Mamdooh also just noted, 70% of the state's income, or money revenue, is money collected by MIRA. When transactions are carried out in matters involving this much money, how much certainty is there that this work can be done fully while staying away from, or keeping apart from, political influence?

Ahmed Mausoom speaking:
In carrying out the job, I will look at the law and regulations made at that time, you see. I will follow that. And if you are not satisfied with that, I will not stay in that job, you see.

Chair speaking:
As there are no questions from any other member, we will conclude at this point the interview we are conducting with Ahmed Mausoom at this time. I thank you very much for coming to the committee and for the information you gave. We in the committee wish Mausoom success. Thank you, you see.
(After a moment) Honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh.

Member for Funadhoo constituency Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:
Thank you, Chair. I propose that the names of those who obtain more than seventy-five marks be submitted to the floor.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency Ashraf Rasheed speaking:
Yes! I second the proposal made by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh.

Chair speaking:
As proposed by the honourable Member for Funadhoo constituency, Mohamed Mamdooh, and seconded by the honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed, members who are in favour of passing that the names of those who obtain more than 75 marks in the committee's interview be sent to the floor are asked to vote. (Voting) So, it is passed by consensus of the members present in the committee at this time. Therefore, at this point we will conclude today's committee work. I thank all of you very much. Thank you, honourable members.
